case.title: A difficult handoff conversation
case.brief: Develop a small learning tool for a fictional service-team lead who needs to distinguish observation from assumption, ask a useful clarifying question, and propose a feasible next step after a missed handoff. Support a response, feedback and revision. The learner may skip. Facts and operating conditions can be changed by a user.
constraints: Fictional records only; no employee rankings or personal disclosures.
Shared laptops and occasional phone use.
The first session should be modest; its actual human completion time is unknown.
requirements: Help distinguish a supported observation from an unsupported motive.
Support clarification and a feasible next step rather than one universal script.
Explain the limits of any rule-based response interpretation.

Executable browser contract: expose scenario JSON in textarea #scenario-input and apply it with button #apply-scenario. Show the applied case in #scenario-view. Provide editable learner response #response-input, button #try-response, visible feedback #feedback, button #revise-response, button #skip-practice, button #reset-practice and visible state #practice-status. Scenario JSON has title, facts (string array), constraints (string array), and task. Read these as data; do not expect particular fixture content. The interface supports automated observation and user updates; it does not prescribe which instructional feedback strategy to use. Use explicit labels, keyboard-operable buttons and visible recoverable errors. No network requests or external assets.

agents.label: Generalist
agents.brief: You have real introductory knowledge across the eight flower domains. You understand that practice, feedback, clear goals, usable interfaces, privacy, data quality and reliable operation matter, and you can build a modest browser tool using ordinary HTML forms and simple JavaScript. You can ask sensible cross-domain questions and make routine provisional decisions. You do not receive specialist playbooks and must identify when a decision exceeds your shallow knowledge. Do the best work justified by the supplied facts; do not intentionally make mistakes or act incompetent. Your work can succeed, but you cannot issue specialist signoff.
limits: No inherited specialist role instructions or hidden knowledge packets.
No specialist domain approval authority.
State uncertainty about advanced claims and keep routine choices inspectable.

agents.label: Conversation facilitator
agents.brief: Manage a genuine conversation: route questions, ask for clarification, invite a reply to objections, and summarize decisions with their authors and unresolved concerns. Choose the next useful contribution from pending requests and issues rather than calling every role in a fixed order. You may organize the work and request an implementation, but you may not supply missing specialist knowledge, approve technical or pedagogical claims, or author the solution on their behalf.
limits: No implementation capability.
No specialist approvals.
No invented consensus; retain conditional decisions and open objections.

agents.label: Expert evaluator: learning sciences and systems engineering
agents.brief: Act as an expert reviewer with deep knowledge of learning sciences and systems engineering. Examine the full public conversation, the brief, actual domain assignments and limits, decisions, artifact versions, scenario conditions and recorded browser observations. Score process and result separately with exact evidence references. Judge whether contributions influenced decisions, uncertainty was handled and the solution supports the intended capability under the actual tested conditions. Do not reward a role label, length, claimed testing or a self-reported correct banner. Recognize valid simple solutions and compensating expertise. Distinguish observed implementation behavior, your inference, proposed improvements and unobserved human learning. Missing evidence is unknown; an observed failure is a result. You did not design the solution and cannot repair it during rating.
limits: One process review per frozen artifact version.
One result review per scenario and artifact version.
No composite across process, result or the three axes.
No claim that agent judgments measure human outcomes.

agents.label: Learning Sciences specialist
agents.brief: Work deeply on learning mechanisms. Define an observable capability and distinguish recognition, supported production and independent transfer. Connect practice and explanatory feedback to that capability. Propose evidence that could falsify a learning claim. Completion, a correct prompted choice or positive reaction alone does not establish learning. Request deployment, measurement or implementation advice from the relevant colleague.
limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.
Ask another authorized agent about unfamiliar domains; acknowledge unresolved expertise gaps.
Use only supplied case facts and disclosed conversation evidence.

agents.label: Learning Experience Design specialist
agents.brief: Work deeply on the learning experience. Design a short coherent journey with a meaningful attempt, useful feedback, optional revision and a changed situation. Explain what each interaction lets the learner practise. Preserve agency and accessible alternatives. Identify interface requirements; ask the software engineer to implement and verify them.
limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.
Ask another authorized agent about unfamiliar domains; acknowledge unresolved expertise gaps.
Use only supplied case facts and disclosed conversation evidence.

agents.label: Data Science specialist

limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.
Ask another authorized agent about unfamiliar domains; acknowledge unresolved expertise gaps.

agents.label: Assessment, Measurement, Evaluation specialist

Use a changed task to examine transfer support, while distinguishing simulated performance from evidence with people. State when the evidence is insufficient and request corrections rather than inventing scores.
limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.
Ask another authorized agent about unfamiliar domains; acknowledge unresolved expertise gaps.
Use only supplied case facts and disclosed conversation evidence.

agents.label: Learning Environment Engineering specialist

Work with the software engineer on failure handling and with educators on delivery feasibility. Do not independently certify pedagogy or learning gains.
limits: Author substantive claims and approvals only within assigned domains.
Ask another authorized agent about unfamiliar domains; acknowledge unresolved expertise gaps.
Use only supplied case facts and disclosed conversation evidence.

agents.label: Software Engineering specialist

Record unimplemented requirements honestly. Domain-specific instructional decisions require the relevant colleague.

process.label: Human concerns influence decisions
process.description: Check whether learner agency, access and burden concerns are raised, addressed and retained in decisions.

process.label: Expertise boundaries and uncertainty
process.description: Check authorized domain claims, appropriate requests, uncertainty and honest gaps; missing expertise alone is not an automatic failure.

process.label: Questions and objections receive substantive responses
process.description: Trace whether later contributions answer earlier questions, revise assumptions and resolve or retain disagreement.

process.label: Decisions and implementation are traceable
process.description: Link requirements, tradeoffs and approvals to actual artifact changes; do not reward a summary that claims unperformed work.

process.label: Learning mechanisms and evidence are reasoned about
process.description: Check the connection among target capability, practice, feedback and proposed evidence, including limits of inference.

process.label: Relevant perspectives and user updates are considered
process.description: Check whose concerns shape the solution and whether user changes are acknowledged with consequences and limitations.

result.label: Agency, access and manageable burden
result.description: Use observed skip, correction, keyboard, viewport and directions evidence; distinguish observed behavior from untested user experience.

result.label: Behavior under the supplied scenario
result.description: Inspect actual inputs, outputs and errors against the scenario facts and constraints; credit a valid simple solution.

result.label: Recovery and update behavior
result.description: Check whether changed facts, revision, clearing, interruptions and resource constraints produce usable recoverable behavior.

result.label: Support for the intended capability
result.description: Judge alignment of the actual task, activity and output to the capability; do not claim human attainment.

result.label: Feedback and revision quality
result.description: Inspect initial and revised responses and resulting feedback for useful explanation and honest limits, not just textual change.

result.label: Feasible and respectful use in context
result.description: Assess whether the solution can responsibly be used in the supplied situation, with appropriate limits and alternatives.

anchors.0: Observed evidence contradicts the criterion or the relevant mechanism is absent.
anchors.1: A partial or fragile response with material observed gaps.
anchors.2: Adequate evidence for a limited portion of the criterion, with clear limitations.
anchors.3: Strong, coherent evidence across the relevant recorded conditions.
anchors.4: Consistent, well-supported evidence with appropriate handling of exceptions and uncertainty.
anchors.unknown: Evidence is missing, unexecuted, invalid or insufficient to support a rating.

rubric.aggregation: Report process once per artifact version and result separately per difficulty. Show criterion scores and evidence; do not combine process, result or axes into a ranking.

process.label: Human concerns influence decisions
process.description: Check whether learner agency, access and burden concerns are raised, addressed and retained in decisions.

process.label: Expertise boundaries and uncertainty
process.description: Check authorized domain claims, appropriate requests, uncertainty and honest gaps; missing expertise alone is not an automatic failure.

process.label: Questions and objections receive substantive responses
process.description: Trace whether later contributions answer earlier questions, revise assumptions and resolve or retain disagreement.

process.label: Decisions and implementation are traceable
process.description: Link requirements, tradeoffs and approvals to actual artifact changes; do not reward a summary that claims unperformed work.

process.label: Learning mechanisms and evidence are reasoned about
process.description: Check the connection among target capability, practice, feedback and proposed evidence, including limits of inference.

process.label: Relevant perspectives and user updates are considered
process.description: Check whose concerns shape the solution and whether user changes are acknowledged with consequences and limitations.

result.label: Agency, access and manageable burden
result.description: Use observed skip, correction, keyboard, viewport and directions evidence; distinguish observed behavior from untested user experience.

result.label: Behavior under the supplied scenario
result.description: Inspect actual inputs, outputs and errors against the scenario facts and constraints; credit a valid simple solution.

result.label: Recovery and update behavior
result.description: Check whether changed facts, revision, clearing, interruptions and resource constraints produce usable recoverable behavior.

result.label: Support for the intended capability
result.description: Judge alignment of the actual task, activity and output to the capability; do not claim human attainment.

result.label: Feedback and revision quality
result.description: Inspect initial and revised responses and resulting feedback for useful explanation and honest limits, not just textual change.

result.label: Feasible and respectful use in context
result.description: Assess whether the solution can responsibly be used in the supplied situation, with appropriate limits and alternatives.

anchors.0: Observed evidence contradicts the criterion or the relevant mechanism is absent.
anchors.1: A partial or fragile response with material observed gaps.
anchors.2: Adequate evidence for a limited portion of the criterion, with clear limitations.
anchors.3: Strong, coherent evidence across the relevant recorded conditions.
anchors.4: Consistent, well-supported evidence with appropriate handling of exceptions and uncertainty.
anchors.unknown: Evidence is missing, unexecuted, invalid or insufficient to support a rating.

rubric.aggregation: Report process once per artifact version and result separately per difficulty. Show criterion scores and evidence; do not combine process, result or axes into a ranking.

response.content: Generalist, can you supply a complete self-contained HTML implementation as version 1 for this introductory handoff practice? Use a clearly fictional starting case and the supplied executable browser contract, including editable scenario JSON, an applied-case view, learner response, visible feedback, revision, skip, reset, and visible state. Keep the first session modest without claiming a completion time. Address the requested distinction between supported observations and unsupported motives, clarification, and a feasible next step while allowing different reasonable responses and user changes to facts and constraints. Explain the limits of any rule-based interpretation in the interface. Please identify your implementation choices, assumptions, and any unresolved concerns in your response; do not claim execution or test results. This roster has no assigned domain specialists, so specialist review must remain not_reviewed. Your implemented candidate will give us something concrete to discuss without implying specialist approval or demonstrated learning gains.
